The '''O'reenians''' were the inhabitants of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[O'reen]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]; although originally [[Human/Legends|Humans]], they eventually evolved into a distinct [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[near-Human]]s. The species appeared similar to Humans physically with the exception of [[Color/Legends|orange]]-hued skin. Their society and culture, on the other hand, were unique in that the O'reenians were divided into several distinct castes based upon [[Army/Legends|military]] service. O'reenians who served in the military for six or more [[Standard year/Legends|years]] were granted the rights and privileges of citizenship, while those who did not were relegated to menial occupations of the sort generally carried out by [[Droid/Legends|droids]] on worlds more technologically advanced than O'reen. Only [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] occupied a social position below non-citizens. A military dictator known as the [[Magnus (title)|Magnus]] ruled the O'reenian government and commanded its military. The system made O'reenian society highly regimented and disciplined, with an emphasis on martial prowess. Indeed, even O'reenian [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] wore [[Blaster/Legends|sidearms]] while at work.

Although they were descended from colonists sent to O'reen by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in the aftermath of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], the location of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] in the Unknown Regions kept the O'reenians isolated and self-sufficient for millennia. Through several chance encounters with offworlders, the O'reenians realized that their technology had fallen behind that of the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], and the government implemented a policy of raiding nearby [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] to take weapons and devices that O'reenian researchers could then reverse-engineer. These missions, normally carried out by [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] in the [[O'reen Star Corps|O'reenian Star Corps]], afforded the species a sense of protection against what they perceived as outside threats. Government policies of the Galactic Republic and the O'reenians alike regularly maintained that keeping the species isolated was the most beneficial course of action; nevertheless, during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Unidentified Magnus (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Magnus]] adopted a policy of potentially taking advantage of the conflict to expand O'reen's sphere of influence.

==Biology and appearance==
Although originally mainline [[Human/Legends|Humans]], the O'reenians evolved into [[near-Human]]s,<ref name="UR" /> with an anatomy that mimicked that of mainline Humans in most ways. That is, each O'reenian had a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body, with two [[Limb/Legends|arms]] with five-fingered hands, two legs, and a head; likewise, their face featured two [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], two eyebrows, a [[Nose/Legends|nose]], two [[Ear/Legends|ears]], and a [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]].<ref name="AFC" /> The major distinctions between the two species were the O'reenians' [[Color/Legends|orange]]-tinted skin and black eyes.<ref name="UR" /> O'reenians tended to have dark-brown hair. At least some [[Gender/Legends|males]] of the [[Species/Legends|species]] kept their hair close-cropped, while others sported short goatees.<ref name="AFC" />

==Society and culture==
O'reenian society was highly militarized and stratified. At the top of the social structure was the [[Magnus (title)|Magnus]], who ruled the species's [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[O'reen]], as a military dictator and supreme military [[Commander/Legends|commander]].<ref name="UR" /> Below the ruler were the [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] in the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] militia, a group who were afforded all rights and privileges of citizenship after a period of service of at least six [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. Near the bottom of the social ladder were civilians, who had few rights; such individuals had little choice but to work for the planetary government as indentured laborers. Another non-martial class of O'reenians were those who were officially [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] to social superiors. The only group regarded even more dimly than civilians and slaves were soldiers who were dishonorably discharged from the [[Army/Legends|army]] for shirking duty. The punishment for such dereliction was the loss of all rights and mandatory [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] from any [[City/Legends|settlement]] on O'reen. The organization of O'reenian society into such clearly demarcated castes encouraged disgruntlement among the lower classes, and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|rebellions]] were common over the species's history&mdash;though rarely successful.<ref name="UR" />

Although non-O'reenians were exceedingly rare on O'reen, the species's society allowed offworlders to enjoy the privileges of citizenship through military service or by proving membership in the military of another group. Outsiders who had not done so were regarded as civilians, with rights equivalent to that class of O'reenians. Non-O'reenians who did not belong to a military organization suffered severely curtailed mobility on the world.<ref name="UR" />

Within the military class, O'reenians were further stratified according to [[Military rank/Legends|rank]]. As supreme commander of the armed forces, the Magnus was elected by a council of his or her peers. The leader received a personal detail of four elite [[Bodyguard/Legends|guards]] for protection and had the ability to rally the O'reenian military to action when necessary.<ref name="UR" /> Another military faction was the [[O'reen Star Corps]], a unit of [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] who patrolled the [[O'reen system/Legends|O'reen system]] and protected it from outside threats. Unless outsiders received proper clearance, the Star Corps refused them access to the planet. A defensive [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] remained in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around O'reen at all times.<ref name="AFC" />

Life for the O'reenians was highly regulated and disciplined. O'reenians learned combat and military skills from an early age so that every O'reenian could act as a competent soldier when necessary.<ref name="UR" /> Even [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] were highly militarized; [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]] researchers carried small sidearms under their white lab coats.<ref name="AFC" /> All O'reenians were more perceptive and fit than a comparable Human, but those O'reenians who were officially part of the planet's military had to show ideological commitment and keep themselves in peak physical condition.<ref name="UR" /> The soldier's life taught an O'reenian military protocol; indeed, lack of such knowledge brought contempt upon many civilian O'reenians.<ref name="AFC" /> Criminals were exceedingly rare in O'reenian society and tended to remain within the fogs that marked the outskirts of civilization.<ref name="UR" />

[[File:Oreen-TUR.jpg|thumb|left|O'reenian settlements were located atop tall, flat, natural landforms.]]
Overall, the O'reenians had access only to relatively primitive technology; they lagged behind much of the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. For instance, most of the tasks performed by [[Droid/Legends|droids]] in the rest of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] fell to O'reenian civilians instead.<ref name="UR" /> Still, the species did have access to items such as [[Datapad/Legends|datapads]] and [[cargo lifter]]s.<ref name="AFC" /> The exception was weaponry. By raiding nearby [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], the military gained access to advanced weapons and armaments, which it then analyzed and adopted. Such bellicose invasions of nearby areas allowed for a robust and advanced array of armaments, which included [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] weapons, [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight drives]], [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generators]] for [[Starship/Legends|starships]],<ref name="UR" /> [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]], and [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drives]].<ref name="AFC" /> Security [[Satellite/Legends|satellites]] filled the planet's orbit and provided advanced warning of attack, and [[Space mine/Legends|orbital defense mines]] presented invisible, target-seeking obstacles to any outsiders with aggressive intent or who lacked the proper [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder codes]].<ref name="UR" />

O'reenian settlements were situated atop towering, flat, natural mesas and plateaux. Their buildings were made of stone and often reached precipitous heights. Such cities tended to be relatively isolated from one another because thick fog that enshrouded O'reen made travel in the wilds dangerous. The planetary [[Capital/Legends|capital]] was [[Fort Maximus]], the most heavily [[Garrison/Legends|garrisoned]] city on the planet. The capital was designed to withstand a siege even for several years, and it housed arms factories protected in underground bunkers. The Magnus lived in an [[Magnus's estate|estate]] at the heart of the city, and most of the populace of Fort Maximus was made up of citizen-soldiers. [[Epsilon Garrison]] was similar in that it was more of a military base than a city, although it did support a large [[Farm/Legends|farming]] community that provided food for the nearby garrisons and for the soldiers stationed at Fort Maximus. The large number of civilians at Epsilon Garrison proved one of the more rebellious in O'reenian society, although the farmers tended to rebel through non-violent protest. [[Orbital Deployment Center]] was another city; its purpose was to operate and monitor the network of satellites that orbited O'reen to spot threats from afar and to [[Spy/Legends|spy]] on nearby areas of the galaxy to identify possible targets for raiding.<ref name="UR" />

Although O'reen was located just beyond the borders of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] within the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], the O'reenians were a tough and self-sufficient people with little concern for the broader galaxy. Their planet had no exports, although the people did import military weaponry.<ref name="UR" /> Indeed, the species was somewhat distrustful and even afraid of [[Alien/Legends|aliens]].<ref name="AFC" /> Still, O'reenian concept of military conduct included the notion that pre-emptive attacks on other groups were sometimes justified, so the species presented a threat to nearby [[Star system/Legends|systems]];<ref name="UR" /> for instance, the Star Corps raided nearby systems from time to time.<ref name="AFC" />

The [[O'reenian language|language]] spoken by the species was derived from an old dialect of [[Bocce/Legends|Bocce]]. Even after the two [[Language/Legends|languages]] had diverged, they remained largely intelligible with one another.<ref name="UR" /> Some O'reenians also learned to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] and [[Minnisiat/Legends|Minnisiat]].<ref name="AFC" />

==History==
===Colonization===
After the conclusion of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]<ref name="UR" /> in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] initiated a program of military colonization whereby [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]] were established in areas of [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] beyond the borders of [[Galactic community|galactic civilization]]. The plans for the program called for such colonies to be fully supported with Republic matériel and [[Trooper/Legends|troops]] and full two-way communication via the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]]. Nevertheless, the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] rejected the original proposal as too expensive. The Republic scaled down the project to instead seed self-sufficient colonies that would still offer some degree of protection against future threats. The Republic asked for volunteers to colonize twelve identified worlds, but the number of volunteers was sufficient only for five, O'reen among them.<ref name="UR" />

Shortly after the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]],<ref name="AFC" /> which concluded in [[3996 BBY]],<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the Human ancestors of the O'reenians thus traveled to O'reen under the auspices of the Republic's program.<ref name="UR" /> With its location in the southwestern quadrant of the galaxy,<ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> O'reen was chosen as a bulwark against an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extragalactic]] force that was feared to threaten the galaxy at the time. A network of satellites was placed in the planet's orbit to allow the O'reenians to monitor nearby systems. However, the threat never materialized. Over [[Time/Legends|time]], four of the Republic's fortress colonies failed entirely, leaving only O'reen as a success. However, financial trouble eventually forced the Republic to completely cut ties to O'reen and its inhabitants.<ref name="UR" />

O'reens vast resources provided the raw materials for the O'reenians to survive on their own. During the rule of the [[Unidentified Republic bureaucrat's son|son]] of a [[Unidentified Republic bureaucrat|dandyish Republic functionary]], a military [[Officer/Legends|officer]] and starship [[Captain/Legends|captain]] named [[Magnus (starship captain)|Magnus]] took over the government of O'reen in a [[Blood/Legends|bloodless]] coup d'état. With widespread public support, Magnus and his [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]] introduced a new lifestyle based on military discipline and widespread martial training. "Magnus" became more than a family name; it became the title of the supreme ruler of O'reen and its O'reenian people.<ref name="UR" />

With time, the O'reenians forgot their ties to the Galactic Republic and the circumstances that had led to the settling of their world. Their society stratified into castes, and laws were passed that granted citizenship only to those who served in the military for at least six years. Non-citizens were thus thrust into menial roles. The O'reenians eventually became a distinct species as well, resembling Humans except for their orange-hued skin and dark eyes. A language derived from an archaic form of Bocce became the species's main tongue.<ref name="UR" />

===Isolationism===
Several centuries before the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the O'reenians made contact with the outside galaxy once again when a corporate [[Scout ship/Legends|exploration vessel]] found O'reen. The offworlders tried to claim the planet for their [[Unidentified corporation (O'reen discovery)|corporation]] through a display of technological superiority, but the O'reenians responded with force and took control of the strangers' starship. The encounter convinced the [[Unidentified Magnus (scout encounter)|Magnus]] that O'reen was vulnerable to technologically superior and aggressive forces from afar. He ordered the planet's scientists to reverse-engineer the ship to improve the capabilities of the O'reenian military. The O'reenians then embarked on a program of sending soldiers and [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] on secret raids on nearby planets, during which further technological advances were sought. Over time, the O'reenians began to reach technological parity with the rest of the galaxy in military hardware. Nevertheless, O'reenian leaders were cautious to keep the location of O'reen completely secret from the targets of such raids.<ref name="UR" />

During the Clone Wars,<ref name="UR" /> a conflict fought between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] from [[22 BBY/Legends|22]] to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="EA" /> the O'reenians were faced with another threat when a [[Unidentified Republic military exploration ship|Republic military exploration ship]] found the planet during a search for Confederate supply planets. The O'reenians took the crew captive and enslaved most of them. The [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Morningfire]] later arrived, supported by the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] of [[Vornskr Company]], to rescue the exploration crew. The [[Unidentified Magnus (Clone Wars rescue)|Magnus]] ordered the military to resist the invasion, but the ruler died during the [[Rescue on O'reen|assault]]. The [[Unidentified Magnus (post-Clone Wars rescue)|subsequent Magnus]] advocated further isolation for the O'reenians to avoid further contact with the Republic. Meanwhile, the Galactic Senate voted to keep O'reen isolated from the galaxy to keep the O'reenians from aiding the Separatists and to curtail any expansionism on the part of the planet's people.<ref name="UR" />

The O'reenians remained isolationists until the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] tore through the galaxy<ref name="UR" /> beginning in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> when the [[Unidentified Magnus (Yuuzhan Vong War)|reigning Magnus]] adopted a policy of watching the conflict between the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] from afar, but remaining vigilant against any aggressors, while also keeping an eye out for opportunities to expand O'reen's sphere of influence. After the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Battle of Coruscant]]<ref name="UR" /> in [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> all records of O'reen were lost to the New Republic.<ref name="UR" />

{{RPGseed|O'reenian Hospitality}}
At one point, a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] arrived on O'reen seeking emergency aid. The offworlders evaded the orbital defenses and landed in the wilderness, but an O'reenian military patrol found and impounded the visitors' starship. The spacers infiltrated the city Orbital Deployment Center to recover the ship. When they finally reached the vessel, they made repairs to the ship, entered the vehicle, and lifted off to leave O'reen. However, some O'reenians had remained aboard and tried to force the offworlders to land back on the planet. The strangers overcame their stowaways and left the O'reen system.<ref name="OH 181">{{WizCite|book=The Unknown Regions|story=O'reenian Hospitality}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

{{RPGseed|A Crateful of Smoking Blasters}}
In another incident, an offworld [[Unidentified O'reenian weapons smuggler|O'reenian]] hired a group of spacers to bring a cargo of high-tech weapons and armor to O'reen. However, the [[Agent/Legends|agent]] told the group that the cargo consisted of nothing more than miscellaneous goods and luxury items. The patsies traveled to the O'reen system, evaded O'reenian system security, and landed. O'reenian officials boarded the ship, confiscated the cargo, and arrested the couriers for [[Treason/Legends|treason]] against the Magnus and for [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]]. Only after giving up their on-world [[Unidentified O'reenian contact|contact]] were the offworlders allowed to leave the system&mdash;albeit under escort by O'reenian forces who then set out to arrest the O'reenian smuggler.<ref name="CSB">{{WizCite|book=The Unknown Regions|story=A Crateful of Smoking Blasters}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|A Fool's Charge}}
On yet another occasion, O'reenian forces attacked a vessel in the Outer Rim Territories near the O'reen system. They confiscated a piece of military hardware and carried it back to O'reen for analysis at a [[Unidentified analysis station|research post]] near Orbital Deployment Center. There, scientists began efforts to decipher the codes embedded in the foreign devices, and an [[Unidentified O'reenian military supervisor|O'reenian military supervisor]] was assigned to protect the hardware until it could be analyzed. Eventually, he received orders to move the cargo to Fort Maximus.<ref name="AFC" />

Later, a group of offworlders traveled to O'reen on the orders of a [[Navy/Legends|navy]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] named [[Amalia]], who wanted the group to investigate the disappearance of the hardware&mdash;a prototype [[Tactical computer/Legends|tactical computer]] and [[tactical data core]] for a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]]&mdash;and recover it. The O'reenians attacked the interlopers upon their arrival in the O'reen system, but the strangers survived the encounter and evaded the rebuilt battle [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] patrolling the system. The offworlders landed on O'reen and infiltrated the analysis center where the stolen Republic hardware was kept. The O'reenian military supervisor detected the intrusion, and in the ensuing [[Skirmish in the Orbital Deployment Center analysis station|skirmish]], a dozen O'reenian researchers were bested by the offworlders, who also recovered the data core. The supervisor's [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] revealed the orders to move the items to Fort Maximus, so the offworlders pretended to do just that. However, they instead fled to their ship and escaped the planet and star system.<ref name="AFC" />
{{Endgame}}

The O'reenians remained isolated from the galaxy as late as [[137 ABY]].<ref name="EA" />

==O'reenians in the galaxy==
With the exception of the Star Corps, which carried out periodic raids on systems near the O'reen system<ref name="AFC" /> to steal weapons and technology, the O'reenians were an isolationist species whose members had little inkling to travel beyond the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of their homeworld. Nevertheless, a few O'reenian exiles abandoned their homeworld altogether and made their way into the greater galaxy. The majority of these expatriates found work as soldiers.<ref name="UR" /> At least one O'reenian smuggled weapons and technology to O'reen by enlisting pilots for hire. In the eyes of the O'reenian government, however, the agent was an outlaw whose activities constituted treason.<ref name="CSB" />

==Behind the scenes==
''[[The Unknown Regions]]'', a sourcebook published by [[Wizards of the Coast]] in [[2010]], describes the O'reenians and their society as part of its entry on the planet O'reen.<ref name="UR" /> The book, written by [[Sterling Hershey]], [[Rodney Thompson]], and [[Daniel Wallace]], includes [[O'reenian Hospitality|three]] [[A Crateful of Smoking Blasters|adventure]] [[A Fool's Charge|outlines]] that allow player characters from the rest of the galaxy to visit O'reen and interact with the O'reenians. However, the sourcebook offers no timeline information to indicate when these adventures take place. The history above includes the events of these scenarios, but their placement within the broader narrative is completely arbitrary. Also in 2010, [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|''The Essential Atlas Online Companion'']], an online supplement to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', placed the O'reen system and provided further context as to the O'reenians' relations with the greater galaxy.<ref name="TEAOC" />
